html:
SMTO-FIL-0002 — Required file or resource was not found

GUID: b563fd25-b1f0-4e58-a57d-8f2b3aec7395
Slug: not-found-error
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO looked for a file, folder or other item it needed, but it isn't where SMTO was told to look. It may have been renamed, moved, deleted, or be on another computer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the spelling of the file or folder name and its full location in your request. A small typo or a wrong folder makes SMTO look in the wrong place.
  2. Open the Execution target menu in the composer and make sure the Gateway for the computer that holds the item is selected. SMTO only looks for files on the computer you selected.
  3. If the item was recently moved or renamed, ask SMTO to list the folder where it should be. The list shows what is really there now, including its current name.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the item and the Task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the name and location you expected, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A FileNotFoundError (ENOENT) was raised, or legacy text matching "no such file" or "not found" was found, for a path or resource the request referenced.

What this means

  • Resolution received FileNotFoundError, or legacy fallback recognized no-such-file/not-found text without a more specific structured identity. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Resolution received FileNotFoundError, or legacy fallback recognized no-such-file/not-found text without a more specific structured identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation's target and structured facts; generic not-found text does not prove a local file was the missing resource.

How to fix it

  • Read the missing path in the technical detail or the Server/Gateway log and confirm it exists on the selected Gateway (or on the Server) with the expected case and working directory. Correct the path or the execution target, then refresh the resource state before retrying.
  • Verify the path and selected target, then refresh current resource state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended resource is available on the selected target.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
